==English== ===Etymology=== From {{der|en|enm|late}}, {{m|enm|lat}}, from {{der|en|ang|læt||slow; slack, lax, negligent; late}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*lat}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lataz||slow, lazy}}. {{surf|+deverbal|en|let}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|laate||late}}, {{cog|frr|leed}}, {{m|frr|leet}}, {{m|frr|lääs||late}}, {{cog|stq|leet||late}}, {{cog|nl|-}}, {{cog|nds-de|laat||late, tardy}}, {{cog|de|lass||lazy, sluggish}}, {{cog|da|lad||languid, lazy, indolent}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|is|latur||lazy}}, {{cog|nb|-}}, {{cog|nn|-}} and {{cog|sv|lat||lazy}}, {{cog|got|𐌻𐌰𐍄𐍃||lazy, slothful}}. {{col-bottom}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/leɪt/|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-late.ogg|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-late.ogg|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/læɪt/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/let/|a=Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/leːt/|a=Wales,non-pane-pain}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=1}} ===Adjective=== {{wikidata lexeme|L8}} {{en-adj|er}} # Near the end of a period of time. #: {{ux|en|The seedlings appeared to be [[coming along]] nicely until a '''late''' frost killed them.}} #: {{ux|en|The meeting is convened for '''late''' morning.}} #: {{ux|en|I've had [[too many]] '''late''' nights recently.}} #: {{ux|en|In [[Southern United States|Southern U.S.]], "evening" is used for middle to '''late''' afternoon.}} # Specifically, near the end of the [[day]]. #: {{ux|en|It was getting '''late''' and I was tired.}} # {{lb|en|usually|not comparable}} Associated with the end of a period. #: {{ux|en|[[Late Latin|'''Late''' Latin]] is less fully inflected than [[Classical Latin]].}} # Not arriving or occurring until [[after]] an [[expect]]ed time. #: {{syn|en|tardy}} #: {{ux|en|The flowers were '''late''' in blooming because of the prolonged cold weather.}} #: {{ux|en|Panos was so '''late''' that he arrived at the meeting after Antonio, who had the excuse of being in hospital for most of the night.}} #: {{ux|en|The heavy snow made all the trains '''late'''.}} # [[levy|Levied]] as a [[surcharge]] on a payment which has not arrived by a specified [[deadline]]. #: {{ux|en|The power company suspended '''late''' fees during the pandemic.}} # Not having had an expected [[menstrual]] [[period]]. #: {{ux|en|I'm '''late''', honey. Could you buy a [[pregnancy test|test]]?}} # {{anchor|deceased}}{{lb|en|not comparable|euphemistic}} Recently [[deceased]], [[dead]]: {{non-gloss|used particularly when speaking of the dead person's actions while alive.}} {{qualifier|Generally must be preceded by a [[possessive]] or an [[article]], commonly "{{l|en|the}}"; see usage notes. Can itself only precede the person's name, never follow it.}} #: {{ux|en|Her '''late''' husband had left her well provided for.}} #: {{ux|en|Mary was entitled to the crown by her '''late''' father’s testament.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|XXIII|181|To Edward […] he was terrible, nerve-inflaming, poisonously asphyxiating. He sat rocking himself in the '''late''' Mr. Churchill's swing chair, smoking and twaddling.}} #* {{quote-av |en|title=w:Monty Python's Flying Circus |episode=Full Frontal Nudity, [[w:Dead Parrot sketch|Dead Parrot sketch]] |author=w:Monty Python |date=1969-12-07 |role=w:Mr Praline |actor=w:John Cleese |passage=This parrot is no more! It has ceased to be! It's expired and gone to meet its maker! This is a '''late''' parrot! It's a stiff! Bereft of life, it rests in peace! If you hadn't nailed it to the perch it would be pushing up the daisies!}} #* {{quote-av|en|date=February 18, 2022|writer=w:Dan Erickson|title={{w|Severance (TV series)|Severance}}|episode=w:Good News About Hell|season=1|number=1|role=Ricken|actor=w:Michael Chernus|passage=Mark’s '''late''' wife, Gemma, was an educator as well. Russian literature.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/fashion/2022/dec/14/hes-not-my-late-husband-iman-talks-of-grief-over-death-of-david-bowie|title=‘He’s not my “late” husband’: Iman speaks of grief over death of David Bowie|date=2022-12-14|author=Nadia Khomami|quotee={{w|Iman (model)|Iman}}|passage=“He is not my ‘'''late''' husband’. He is my husband,” she said, before discussing how the couple had managed to retain their independent identities while together.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018133435/https://www.theguardian.com/fashion/2022/dec/14/hes-not-my-late-husband-iman-talks-of-grief-over-death-of-david-bowie|archivedate=18 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|dated}} Existing or holding some position not long ago, but not now; departed, or gone [[out of office]]. #: {{ux|en|the '''late''' bishop of London}} #: {{ux|en|the '''late''' administration}} #* {{quote-book|en|author=[[w:Edward Reynolds|Edvvard Reynoldes]]|title=A Treatise of the Passions and Facvlties of the Soul of Man. With the severall Dignities and Corruptions thereunto belonging.|location=London|publisher={{...|Printed by}}R. H. for Robert Bostock,{{nb...|dwelling in Saint Pauls Church yard at the Signe of the Kings Head.}}|year=1640|passage=By [[w:Edward Reynolds|{{smc|Edvvard Reynoldes}}]], '''late''' Preacher to the Honorable Society of ''Lincoln’s Inne'': And now Rector of the Church of ''Braunſton'' in ''Northamptonſhire''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1862|author=Mary Elizabeth Braddon|title=Lady Audley's Secret |passage=It was a lonely place enough, even in all its rustic beauty, for so bright a creature as the '''late''' Miss Lucy Graham, but the generous baronet had transformed the interior of the gray old mansion into a little palace for his young wife, and Lady Audley seemed as happy as a child surrounded by new and costly toys.}} # Recent — relative to the noun it modifies. #: {{ux|en|the '''late''' war}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 2|I|i|23|1|{{big|O}}Ld ''Iohn of Gaunt'', time-honoured Lancaſter,
Haſt thou according to thy oath and band
Brought hither ''Henry'' Herford thy bold ſon:
Heere to make good yͤ boiſtrous '''late''' appeale,
Which then our leyſure would not let vs heare,
Againſt the Duke of Norfolke, ''Thomas Mowbray''?}} #* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Robert Frost|chapter=A Hundred Collars|title=w:North of Boston|year=1914|passage={{smc|Lancaster}} bore him—such a little town, / Such a great man. It doesn't see him often / Of '''late''' years, though he keeps the old homestead / And sends the children down there with their mother{{...}}}} # {{lb|en|astronomy}} Of a star or class of stars, cooler than the sun. ====Usage notes==== * {{sense|deceased}} {{m|en||Late}} in this sense qualifies named individuals (in phrases like {{m|en||the late Mary Smith}}). In this sense, it generally is confined to usage with the person's full name, or a title, relationship, etc., that would be adequate by itself to identify the person: {{m|en||the late Mary Smith}}; {{m|en||the late queen}}; {{m|en||his late wife}}; {{m|en||the late Mary, Queen of Scots}}; but in most cases '''not''' {{m|en||the late Mary}}. ====Descendants==== * {{desc|ml|ലേറ്റ്|bor=1}} *
